mainTopic: Which תנא requires both the writing and the signing of a גט to be done לשמה (for the sake of this specific woman)?
overview: The גמרא is looking for a תנא who holds that a גט must be both written לשמה and signed לשמה. At first neither candidate fits. רבי מאיר requires only the signing to be לשמה, which the גמרא proves from the משנה about a גט written on something attached to the ground. רבי אלעזר requires only the writing to be לשמה. Someone suggests that רבי אלעזר might still require signing לשמה מדרבנן. The גמרא rejects this from the משנה of the 'three invalid גיטין', where רבי אלעזר rules that a גט with no signatures at all is fully valid. The גמרא then tries the same idea with רבי מאיר: perhaps he requires the writing לשמה מדרבנן. It challenges this with רב נחמן's report that רבי מאיר accepts even a גט found in the garbage. That quote continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Who requires the signing to be for her sake?
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the גמרא's question: which תנא requires both the writing and the signing to be לשמה?
steps.simpleTranslation: [Who is the תנא who requires the writing to be for her sake and also] the signing to be for her sake?
steps.whatsHappening: These two words finish a question that began just before this point: which תנא holds that both the writing and the signing of a גט must be לשמה? This sets up the search that fills the rest of this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט involves two main acts: writing the document and the witnesses signing it. The גמרא wants a תנא who demands that both acts be done with this particular woman in mind. As we will see, each famous opinion requires only one of the two.

keyTerms.meaning: For her sake, done specifically for this woman
Signing, the witnesses' signatures on the גט
Writing, the writing of the גט document

phrases.english: [and requires] the signing to be for her sake?
phrases.notes: This finishes the question from the line before: who needs both the writing and the signing to be לשמה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a question begun before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who requires both כתיבה לשמה and חתימה לשמה.

steps.title: רבי מאיר requires only the signing for her sake
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר can't be the source, because he requires only the signing to be לשמה, not the writing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is רבי מאיר, he requires the signing to be for her sake, but he does not require the writing to be for her sake!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first candidate, רבי מאיר, and says he does not fit. He cares only about the signing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We need a תנא who requires both writing and signing לשמה. רבי מאיר requires only one of them, the signing. So he cannot be the source, and the proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who holds that the signing is the key act of a גט
If, introducing a possible candidate
Requires

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Meir –
he requires the signing [for her sake], he does not require the writing [for her sake]!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי מֵאִיר – חֲתִימָה בָּעֵי, כְּתִיבָה לָא בָּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first candidate answer to the question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי מאיר is the תנא who requires both acts to be לשמה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר requires only the signing to be לשמה, so he doesn't match a view that requires both.

steps.title: Proof from a גט written on something attached to the ground
steps.stepSummary: A משנה rules that a גט written on something attached to the ground, then cut off and signed, is valid. This shows the signing is what counts for רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: One may not write a גט on something attached to the ground. But if he wrote it on something attached to the ground, then cut it off, signed it, and gave it to her, it is valid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that רבי מאיר does not care about the writing stage. It brings a משנה where the writing was done in a problematic way, yet the גט is valid because the signing was done properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing on something attached to the ground is not allowed. Still, if the item is detached before it is signed, the גט works. This shows the signing is the act that really makes the גט, so the writing stage does not need to be לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Attached to the ground, like a leaf still on a tree
He detached it, cut it off
Valid

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the writing doesn't matter at all. One may not write on something attached to the ground in the first place. The point is only that, after the fact, the signing is what makes the גט work.

phrases.english: As we learned: One may not write [a גט]
on something attached to the ground.
If he wrote it on something attached to the ground,
detached it, signed it, and gave it to her – it is valid!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim made about רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר requires only the signing, not the writing, to be done properly and לשמה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a גט written on something attached to the ground.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר requires only the writing for her sake
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר can't be the source either, because he requires only the writing to be לשמה, not the signing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is רבי אלעזר, he requires the writing to be for her sake, but he does not require the signing to be for her sake!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the second candidate, רבי אלעזר, and finds the opposite problem: he cares only about the writing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר is the mirror image of רבי מאיר. He requires the writing to be לשמה but not the signing. Again, neither candidate matches a view that requires both.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with רבי מאיר about which stage of the גט matters most
Does not require

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Elazar –
he requires the writing [for her sake], he does not require the signing [for her sake]!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר – כְּתִיבָה בָּעֵי, חֲתִימָה לָא בָּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the second candidate after רבי מאיר was ruled out.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי אלעזר is the תנא who requires both acts to be לשמה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר requires only the writing to be לשמה, so he too doesn't match a view that requires both.

steps.title: Maybe רבי אלעזר requires signing for her sake by rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: A suggested defense: רבי אלעזר doesn't require signing לשמה מדאורייתא, but he does require it מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: really it is רבי אלעזר. When he said signing does not need to be for her sake, he meant by Torah law, but by rabbinic law he does require it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a way to save the idea that רבי אלעזר is the source. It splits the rule into Torah law and rabbinic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is that רבי אלעזר's leniency about signing applies only מדאורייתא. מדרבנן he would still demand signing לשמה, which would make him the תנא who requires both. The next step tests this suggestion.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say, introducing a possible answer
Really, actually, keeping the original idea
By Torah law
By rabbinic law

phrases.english: And if you would say
actually it is Rabbi Elazar,
and when Rabbi Elazar does not require
the signing to be for her sake – that is by Torah law,
but by rabbinic law – he does require it;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a defense against the challenge to רבי אלעזר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the level of the law: Torah law versus rabbinic law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר does not require signing לשמה at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps he does not require it מדאורייתא but does require it מדרבנן.

steps.title: The rabbinic-law suggestion is rejected
steps.stepSummary: Against the suggestion: in the case of the 'three rabbinically invalid גיטין', רבי אלעזר does not require signing לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are the three גיטין that are invalid by rabbinic law, and there רבי אלעזר does not require the signing to be for her sake!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the suggestion from the previous step. It points to a case about rabbinic validity where רבי אלעזר clearly does not care about signing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי אלעזר required signing לשמה מדרבנן, he would be strict in a case dealing with rabbinic validity. But in the משנה of the three rabbinically invalid גיטין, he does not demand proper signing at all. The proof comes in the next two steps.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, introducing a counter-source
Invalid by rabbinic law

phrases.english: But there are three גיטין that are invalid by rabbinic law,
and Rabbi Elazar does not require
the signing to be for her sake!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense offered in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבי אלעזר requires signing לשמה מדרבנן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In a case that is about rabbinic validity, רבי אלעזר still does not require signing.

steps.title: The משנה of the three invalid גיטין
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists three גיטין that are invalid מדרבנן, though a child born from a later marriage is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: Three גיטין are invalid, but if she remarried, the child is valid. These are: a גט he wrote in his own handwriting with no witnesses on it; a גט with witnesses but no date; and a גט with a date but only one witness. These are the three invalid גיטין, and if she remarried, the child is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה it just mentioned. It starts with the first opinion, which lists the three flawed גיטין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these גיטין has a flaw in its signatures or date, so חכמים call it invalid. Yet if the woman remarried, the child is כשר, which shows the גט works מדאורייתא. That is why these are called 'invalid by rabbinic law.'

keyTerms.meaning: She married, here meaning she remarried
The child is valid, not a ממזר
His own handwriting
A date written in the גט
One witness

phrases.english: As we learned: Three גיטין are invalid,
but if she married [another man], the child is valid:
phrases.notes: Since the child is not a ממזר, she was really divorced, so the גט works by Torah law.

phrases.english: he wrote it in his own handwriting
and there are no witnesses [signed] on it,

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ עָלָיו עֵדִים וְאֵין בּוֹ זְמַן,
phrases.english: there are witnesses on it but no date in it,
there is a date in it
but there is only one witness on it –
these are the three invalid גיטין,
and if she married – the child is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה גִּיטִּין פְּסוּלִין, וְאִם נִיסַּת הַוָּלָד כָּשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source referred to in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That the three גיטין are invalid only מדרבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of the three invalid גיטין.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: a גט with no signatures is fully valid
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that a גט handed over in front of witnesses is valid even with no signatures, because signatures are only for תיקון העולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: Even if there are no witnesses signed on it, as long as he gave it to her in front of witnesses, it is valid, and she can collect even from property that was sold. The witnesses sign the גט only for the betterment of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the key part of the משנה. רבי אלעזר says that signatures are not needed at all for the גט to be valid, which completes the rejection from step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר, what makes a גט work is handing it over in front of witnesses, and signatures are only a protective measure. If he allows a גט with no signatures at all to be fully valid, he certainly does not require signatures to be לשמה, even מדרבנן. So the suggestion in step 5 fails, and the next step tries the same idea with רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of witnesses
She collects (payment)
Property that is under a lien and has since been sold to others
The betterment of the world, a protective rabbinic purpose

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר requires only the signing to be לשמה, and רבי אלעזר requires only the writing to be לשמה. Since רבי אלעזר holds a גט with no signatures can be fully valid, he cannot require signing לשמה even מדרבנן. Step 9 next tries to make רבי מאיר the תנא who requires both.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the basic disagreement behind much of מסכת גיטין. Does the signing make the גט, or does handing it over in front of witnesses?

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו עֵדִים –
phrases.english: Even though there are no witnesses [signed] on it –
but he gave it to her in front of witnesses;
it is valid, and she collects [her כתובה] even from sold property.
For the witnesses do not sign the גט
except for the betterment of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה and gives the decisive evidence for the rejection in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר does not require signing at all, and so certainly not signing לשמה, even מדרבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר's ruling in the משנה of the three invalid גיטין.

steps.title: Maybe the משנה follows רבי מאיר, who requires writing for her sake rabbinically
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה is רבי מאיר. He doesn't require the writing to be לשמה מדאורייתא, but he does require it מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה follows רבי מאיר. When רבי מאיר says writing לשמה is not required, he means not by Torah law. By rabbinic law he does require it.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רבי אלעזר was ruled out, the גמרא now tries to make the משנה fit רבי מאיר instead. It uses the same Torah-law versus rabbinic-law idea it used before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר requires the signing to be לשמה by Torah law, but not the writing. The suggestion is that he still requires the writing לשמה מדרבנן. If so, he would require both, which is exactly what the משנה needs.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather / but instead: introduces a new attempt after the last one failed
Writing the גט specifically for this woman
By Torah law
By rabbinic law

steps.confusionAlert: This is the mirror image of the earlier suggestion. For רבי אלעזר, the rabbinic add-on was the signing. For רבי מאיר, the rabbinic add-on is the writing.

phrases.english: Rather, it is רבי מאיר,
phrases.notes: He means the משנה follows רבי מאיר's view.

phrases.english: and when רבי מאיר does not require
writing for her sake, that is by Torah law;
by rabbinic law he does require it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רבי אלעזר suggestion was rejected in Steps 6-8, the גמרא goes back to רבי מאיר and applies the same rabbinic-level defense to him.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting levels of law: Torah law versus rabbinic law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר doesn't require writing לשמה at all, so he can't be the source of the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He doesn't require it only by Torah law. Rabbinically he does, so he could match the משנה's demand for both.

steps.title: רב נחמן reports that רבי מאיר validates even a גט found in the garbage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the suggestion with רב נחמן's report that רבי מאיר said a גט is fine even if it was found in a garbage heap. The quote continues in the lines that follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב נחמן say that רבי מאיר used to say: even if he found it in a garbage heap...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins attacking the רבי מאיר suggestion with a quote from רב נחמן. The quote is not finished yet; the rest of it comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט found in the garbage was obviously not written for this woman, not even rabbinically. If רבי מאיר accepts such a גט, he does not require writing לשמה even מדרבנן, and Step 9's suggestion falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that: introduces a challenge from a known source
He used to say
He found it
Garbage heap / trash pile

phrases.english: But didn't רב נחמן say,
רבי מאיר used to say:
even if he found it in a garbage heap,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אוֹמֵר הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step directly challenges Step 9's claim that רבי מאיר requires writing לשמה מדרבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 9's claim that רבי מאיר requires writing לשמה at the rabbinic level.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר accepts even a גט found in the garbage, which was never written for this woman. So he cannot require writing לשמה, even מדרבנן.
